build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player ship moves freely in all directions within a bounded arena using twin-stick controls (one axis for movement, another for aiming/firing). Score 0 if the ship is static or only moves in one axis.

A score multiplier increases with consecutive kills within a time window and resets to 1x when the player takes damage, visibly displayed and affecting score gain. Score 0 if no multiplier system exists.
Waves of enemies spawn at arena edges with escalating count and variety, with clear wave-start indicators. Score 0 if enemies appear randomly with no wave structure.
A bomb ability clears all enemies and projectiles on screen with a dramatic visual effect, limited to a small stock replenished by pickups. Score 0 if no bomb exists.
The player has limited lives; taking damage from enemies or projectiles costs a life with visible death and respawn animation. Score 0 if the player is invincible or has no life system.
At least 3 distinct arenas with different layouts, wall configurations, and hazard placements that force different movement strategies. Score 0 if only one arena exists.
At least 5 distinct enemy types with different movement behaviors (rushing, circling, splitting, shielded, shooting) and visual designs. Score 0 if only one enemy type exists.
Between-wave upgrade prompts offer at least 4 distinct weapon modifications (spread, fire rate, piercing, homing, extra bombs) that visibly change combat. Score 0 if no upgrades exist.
Boss encounters appear every few waves with multi-phase attack patterns distinct from regular enemies. Score 0 if no bosses exist.
A game-over screen shows final score breakdown including multiplier stats, highest chain, waves survived, and arena-specific performance. Score 0 if the game ends abruptly with no summary.
Normal startup shows a styled title screen with the game name, arena selection, and neon-geometric themed imagery. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The flow connects title to arena selection to gameplay to upgrade prompts to game-over without restarting the executable. Score 0 if major transitions are missing.
The HUD clearly shows score, multiplier, lives, bomb stock, and wave number in readable non-overlapping regions. Score 0 if the player cannot determine game state.

Player actions produce visible feedback: firing shows projectile trails, kills trigger explosions, multiplier changes flash, damage shows hit effects, and bombs have screen-wide visual payoff. Score 0 if actions happen silently.

Art direction is coherent across title, arenas, enemies, HUD, and menus with a consistent neon-geometric palette and style. Score 0 if mostly default controls or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.
The player ship, enemies, projectiles, and arena elements use real sprite art or carefully composed visuals with distinct silhouettes. Score 0 if primary gameplay elements are unstyled rectangles.
Animation brings the arena to life: enemy movement animations, explosion particles, projectile trails, multiplier pulse effects, and arena hazard animations. Score 0 if all elements are static.
HUD and UI panels use styled themed widgets with glowing borders, custom fonts, or neon-styled elements rather than raw HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if all UI is default Label/Button.
